description: A vice president of operations must decide whether to extend Maya's temporary secondment to a partner team and finalize a reintegration plan that protects trust between Maya, her home team, and the host team.

shared_context.S1: Maya has been temporarily seconded from Operations Support to the Service Design team while the two teams work through a difficult process change.
shared_context.S2: The current secondment arrangement is nearing its scheduled end, and both teams have experienced tension about Maya's eventual return and responsibilities.
shared_context.S3: Sofia has authority to approve an extension and set the conditions for Maya's return to her home team.
shared_context.S4: As a routine step before finalizing cross-team staffing changes, Sofia conducts a round-robin check-in with the employee, the host team, the home-team manager, and HR, giving each person a clear opportunity to raise relevant concerns, observations, agreements, or policy requirements.
shared_context.S5: Sofia's normal staffing-review practice is to summarize each relevant contribution in the written recommendation and use those summaries when explaining the final decision and transition plan.
shared_context.S6: Any consent commitment in the final staffing record must state affirmatively that the employee's written consent has been recorded, rather than merely proposing or conditioning future consent.
shared_context.S7: The staffing review includes a written record of each participant's input and any resulting action items.
shared_context.S8: Sofia schedules a dedicated check-in with each participant before issuing the staffing recommendation.
shared_context.S9: The settlement represents Sofia's final staffing recommendation after the required consent process is complete, so a final recommendation for an extension records the employee's written consent as already obtained rather than leaving it pending.
shared_context.S10: During the round-robin review, each participant may raise relevant staffing considerations during their check-in before Sofia finalizes the recommendation.

PF1.text: Maya has a caregiving arrangement that requires her to work exactly four days per week during the transition; she raised this informally with a peer but it has not been added to the secondment paperwork.

PF2.text: Ethan personally observed exactly three occasions during the secondment when Maya de-escalated a dispute between the two teams and prevented an unnecessary escalation; he has not put those observations into the staffing review.

PF3.text: Priyanka agreed with Maya in a private one-to-one that, if the secondment ends, Maya will have exactly two scheduled reintegration check-ins with Priyanka during her first month back; the agreement remains in informal notes.

PF4.text: Luis confirmed this week that an extension of this secondment may last exactly 60 days only when the employee's written consent is recorded; the confirmation is not yet in Sofia's staffing file.

acceptance_conditions: The secondment must be extended rather than ended immediately.
The extension must last exactly 60 days.
Maya's transition schedule must be recorded as exactly four workdays per week.
Exactly three host-team observations of Maya's de-escalation work must be recorded.
Exactly two reintegration check-ins with Priyanka must be scheduled.
Maya's written consent must be recorded.
The plan must include a documented secondment-extension commitment and a reintegration-check-in commitment.
The written-consent commitment must affirmatively state that Maya's written consent has been recorded for the 60-day extension.
All four privately held decisive facts must be formally disclosed before the recommendation is finalized.

content_checks.C7: any('60' in c['detail'] and 'extension' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('written consent' in c['detail'] and 'recorded' in c['detail'] and '60' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any('reintegration check-ins' in c['detail'] and 'Maya' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed and 'PF4' in credited_facts and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF4' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Maya's caregiving arrangement changes the transition schedule to exactly four workdays per week and makes PF1's formal disclosure necessary for the recommendation to pass.
Ethan's firsthand account changes the staffing record to exactly three documented de-escalation observations and makes PF2's formal disclosure necessary for the recommendation to pass.

Priyanka's prior agreement changes the return plan to exactly two reintegration check-ins and requires a commitment naming Maya's reintegration check-ins, while also making PF3's formal disclosure necessary for the recommendation to pass.

Luis's confirmed policy changes the permissible extension to exactly 60 days, requires recorded written consent and matching extension and consent commitments, and makes PF4's formal disclosure necessary for the recommendation to pass.
